nodes.title: Part 1: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 1. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which AWS service provides a fully managed environment to build, train, and depl?
flashcards.back: Amazon SageMaker is the end-to-end managed ML platform on AWS that covers data labeling, training, tuning, deployment, and monitoring. Rekognition, Comprehend and Glue are higher-level or data-prep services.

flashcards.front: Which Amazon service is purpose-built for generative AI applications using found?
flashcards.back: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that exposes foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Amazon Titan, etc.) through a single serverless API for building generative AI apps.

flashcards.front: A company wants to extract entities, key phrases and sentiment from customer sup?
flashcards.back: Amazon Comprehend is the NLP service that detects entities, key phrases, language, sentiment, and PII in text. Translate handles language translation, Transcribe converts speech to text, and Kendra is enterprise search.

flashcards.front: What is the primary purpose of prompt engineering in generative AI?
flashcards.back: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing the text input (the prompt) so that a foundation model produces accurate, on-task responses without modifying the model's weights. more relevant outputs

nodes.title: Part 2: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 2. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which type of machine learning learns from labeled examples to predict an output?
flashcards.back: Supervised learning trains a model on input-output pairs (labeled data) to predict labels for new inputs. Unsupervised finds structure in unlabeled data; reinforcement learns by reward signals.

flashcards.front: A model performs extremely well on the training set but poorly on unseen data. W?
flashcards.back: Overfitting means the model has memorized the training data including its noise, so it generalizes poorly. Common mitigations: more data, regularization, simpler models, dropout, or early stopping.

flashcards.front: Which AWS service helps developers detect bias and explain ML model predictions?
flashcards.back: SageMaker Clarify provides bias detection on data and models and uses SHAP values for explainability of predictions. Ground Truth handles labeling, Pipelines orchestrates ML workflows, Feature Store stores features.

flashcards.front: Which AWS service converts text to lifelike speech using deep learning?
flashcards.back: Amazon Polly is the text-to-speech (TTS) service. Transcribe is the reverse (speech-to-text), Translate is for language translation, and Lex is for conversational chatbots.

nodes.title: Part 3: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 3. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which AWS Bedrock feature lets you create a managed knowledge base and have a mo?
flashcards.back: Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock implements a managed RAG pipeline: ingest documents, chunk + embed them, store vectors and let models answer grounded questions. Guardrails enforces safety policies; Model Evaluation compares models; Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity.

flashcards.front: Which Bedrock feature helps block harmful content, profanity, prompt injection, ?
flashcards.back: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock allow you to define content filters, denied topics, word filters, sensitive-information filters, and contextual grounding checks for foundation models.

flashcards.front: Which metric is MOST appropriate to evaluate a binary classification model on an?
flashcards.back: On imbalanced datasets, accuracy can be misleading (a model predicting only the majority class still scores high). F1-score balances precision and recall, making it more meaningful. MSE and R^2 are regression metrics.

flashcards.front: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model for AI services such as Amazon Bedrock?
flashcards.back: AWS manages the infrastructure, hardware, and the hosted foundation models. The customer is responsible for how they use the service: input data, prompt design, fine-tuning data, evaluation of outputs and downstream application controls. and evaluating outputs for their use case
